items.title: A Noetherian local ring with geometrically normal formal fibres is Nagata and has the same number of branches as its completion
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a Noetherian local ring (A, m) whose formal fibres are geometrically normal (as happens for excellent or quasi-excellent rings) and concludes both that A is Nagata and that the number of (geometric) branches of A and of its completion A-hat agree (source lines 32230-32239). The proof is a multi-stage reduction. Since a normal ring is reduced, A is Nagata by the Nagata-local-ring lemma; the rest of the proof then establishes that A is a P-ring for the property 'geometrically normal over k' using the formal-fibres lemma, the finite-type-over-a-P-ring proposition and the criterion on maximal ideals, together with the corresponding statement for essentially finite type A-algebras (proof lines 32242-32249). It then reduces to the case where A is a domain: for a minimal prime q one has A-hat/q A-hat = (A/q)-hat and A^h/q A^h = (A/q)^h, so the number of branches of A is the sum over q of the numbers of branches of the quotients, and the same for A-hat (proof lines 32252-32259). The substantive part is the domain case. Letting A' be the integral closure of A in its fraction field K, finiteness of A -> A' follows from Nagata; the number of branches of A is the number of maximal ideals of A', and A'-hat decomposes as A' tensor_A A-hat, which in turn is the product over the maximal ideals m' of A' of the completions (A'_{m'})-hat (proof lines 32262-32271). Because each A'_{m'} is a local ring with geometrically normal formal fibres, each such completion is normal, so the minimal primes of A' tensor_A A-hat are in bijection with the factors of that product (proof lines 32272-32278). Finally, flatness of A -> A-hat gives the inclusions A-hat subset A' tensor_A A-hat subset K tensor_A A-hat, and since the outer rings have the same minimal primes so does the middle one, in a step the author states is a small detail omitted, which finishes the proof (proof lines 32278-32284). The geometric-branches statement is then obtained by applying the branch result to A^{sh}, using that its formal fibres are geometrically normal and that (A^{sh})-hat = ((A-hat)^{sh})-hat (proof lines 32287-32293). The non-routine content is the P-ring reduction and the minimal-prime comparison in the domain case.
